subject: POC trial: model selection & success criteria - Acme Fintech
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acmefin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps — POC trial & model selection (recap + owners)

Hi Sophie — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed plan for the POC so we can get you running in the next 2–3 weeks.

Key goals you called out:
- Improve customer support triage accuracy for Spanish & French inquiries (multilingual)
- Maintain average latency < 250ms for single-turn retrieval+generate path
- Reduce false-positive escalation rate by 30% vs current rules

Proposed success criteria (for the trial):
1) Intent classification accuracy >= 90% on your labeled validation set (English/Spanish/French)
2) Response relevance NDCG@5 improvement >= 15% vs baseline
3) 95th percentile inference latency < 400ms (end-to-end) with batch sizes typical of your traffic
4) No PII leakage incidents; all logs stored per your retention policy (we'll use your VPC config)

Model recommendation for the POC:
- Primary: Llama-2-13B (quantized FP4), tuned with your prompt templates — balances multilingual capabilities and latency when run on our optimized runtime
- Fallback: Mistral-7B or a Llama-2-7B variant (smaller) for cost-sensitive bursts and graceful degradation

Why this combo: Llama-2-13B gives better cross-lingual understanding out of the box for Spanish/French and handles longer context; Mistral/Llama-7B are good fallback options when you need throughput or lower cost. We'll run comparative evals on your sample set during week 1 of the trial.

POC timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize scope, success criteria, and legal/compliance checklist
- Week 1: infra setup, data ingestion (1k labeled examples), baseline runs across candidate models
- Week 2: tuning + rerun evaluations, latency/cost profiling, set up monitoring in Redwood Console
- Week 3: handoff, run-through with your support team, decision meeting

Ownership:
- Marissa (me): POC lead, PM for scope/rdl, weekly syncs
- Ben: deployment + runtime tuning, batching/quantization setup
- Aditya: eval metrics and model-selection experiments; will own the comparison report
- Sophie/Liam (Acme): provide labeled examples, acceptance criteria sign-off, legal/compliance approvals

Next steps (can we confirm by EOD Monday?):
1) Sophie: share 1k labeled examples (sample CSV or Drive link)
2) Acme legal: share standard security questionnaire or confirm SOC2 evidence needs
3) Marissa/Ben/Aditya: provision dedicated trial space and kick off baseline runs once we have data

Attachments: acme_poc_action_plan.xlsx (action plan + timeline), model-comparison-metrics.pdf (initial draft)

Thanks — happy to adjust models if you have a preferred open checkpoint.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0132


From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acmefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmefin.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps — POC trial & model selection (recap + owners)

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications: 
- For multilingual: English and Spanish are highest priority, French is secondary (we have ~12% Spanish volume, 4% French).
- Data: we'll upload a 1k sample CSV to the Drive folder by Monday AM — Liam will own that.
- Legal: we'll need a quick SOC2 evidence package and your standard DPA; I've looped in legal@acmefin.com separately.

One ask on the model side: does Redwood have any prior benchmark numbers (accuracy/latency) comparing Llama-2-13B vs Mistral-7B on multilingual classification tasks? If not, happy to run whatever you suggest.

We'll confirm timeline once legal confirms the DPA. Excited to move forward.

Best,
Sophie
Product Lead, Customer Support Automation
Acme Fintech

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acmefin.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps — POC trial & model selection (recap + owners)

Hi Sophie — quick note on benchmarks. We have internal performance profiles for both checkpoints; I'll summarize the expectations below and Aditya will run the specific evals on your dataset once it's uploaded.

Internal expectations (rough, on Redwood Dedicated hardware with our optimized runtime):
- Llama-2-13B (quantized FP4): intent/classification F1 ~0.88–0.92 on mixed EN/ES datasets; 95p latency ~300–450ms depending on batch and context length; cost: moderate
- Mistral-7B: F1 ~0.82–0.88 on mixed EN/ES; 95p latency ~200–300ms; cost: lower

Plan: run both with your prompts + 1k labeled examples, report per-language metrics (precision/recall/F1), latency P50/P95, and token-cost estimates. We'll also test a small prompt-engineering pass (few-shot) to gauge lift.

I'll prepare a short comparison doc (will attach) and we can review it at the end of Week 1.

Ben
Principal Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acmefin.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps — POC trial & model selection (recap + owners)

Thanks — just got the sample CSV in the Drive (thanks Liam). I'll kick off baseline runs today. Quick notes on eval plan and artifacts you'll get: 
- Artifacts: per-model result CSVs, eval notebook (Colab link), latency profiles, cost-per-1000-requests estimates, confusion matrices per language
- Evaluation metrics: accuracy/precision/recall/F1 per intent, macro-F1 across languages, NDCG for ranking responses where applicable
- Safety checks: PII detection sweep and simple prompt-injection heuristics run on generated outputs

If anyone prefers a different primary metric (e.g., macro-F1 vs weighted-F1), call it out now. Our default for multilingual is macro-F1 so languages with smaller volume aren't drowned out.

I'll attach the initial run results by EOD and propose a short 30-min review Thurs.

— Aditya
Sr. ML Engineer, Eval & Onboarding

From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acmefin.com>
